newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: BoE's Davies says Social Chapter not huge handicap.
newsitem.headline: BoE's Davies says Social Chapter not huge handicap.

text.p: The Deputy Governor of the Bank of England Howard Davies said Monday the European Union's Social Chapter on workers' rights, which the Labour government plans to adopt, was "not a huge handicap" for British firms.

Answering questions at an Argentine banking conference, he said signing up to the Social Chapter did not mean importing "the considerably higher social costs which exist in countries like France and Germany."

Davies said the main elements of the Social Chapter, which was resisted by the Conservative government of John Major but will be adopted by the new Labour government of Prime Minister Tony Blair, were paternity leave and "work councils" in firms.
He said most British companies operating in Europe already had work councils.
"At the moment the social chapter does not have significant impact on British companies. It is not a huge handicap for British companies," said Davies.
However, the Bank of England official said he agreed it "would be a mistake to import those social costs."
Davies was also asked about the prospects for Europe's banking system after the introduction of the single currency planned for January 1999.

He predicted that "inevitably there will be much greater competition between the banking systems in member countries" after the advent of European Monetary Union, because the existence of separate currencies puts up barriers to the expansion of banks beyond their national borders.
The main beneficiaries will be the banking systems of countries like Britain and the Netherlands whose banking industries have cut costs, Davies said.
Those that would suffer most were likely to be countries like Italy and France which "have not modernized themselves or cut costs like elsewhere," he said.
